titulo: Quiz — Who they think they are
introPt: A conversation about a grandmother’s language opens into something larger.
cenario: A family history comes up in conversation.

dialogo.es: Mi abuela hablaba náhuatl, pero ya nosotros no.
dialogo.pt: My grandmother spoke Nahuatl, but we don't anymore.
What part is your family from?

dialogo.es: De un pueblo de Puebla, en la sierra.
dialogo.pt: From a town in Puebla, in the mountains.
And what does that name mean?

perguntas.pergunta: What two ideas was modern Mexican identity built on?
opcoes: Mestizaje and a claimed line back to Tenochtitlan
perguntas.explica: Both were promoted hard by the state after the Revolution.

opcoes: The Constitution recognised Mexico as pluricultural
perguntas.explica: A formal move away from mestizaje as the single story.

perguntas.pergunta: Someone says their family lost a language. What is the better response?
opcoes: Ask where the family is from
perguntas.explica: A visitor verdict grades the family; a question gets the story.

perguntas.pergunta: Why are place names a good way into this topic?
opcoes: Anyone can answer and nobody has to take a position
They are written on every map
perguntas.explica: Half the map is Nahuatl, Maya, Purépecha or Zapotec.

perguntas.pergunta: You hear two people disagree about mestizaje. What should you do?
opcoes: Notice which position you are hearing
Argue for the more inclusive one
Repeat what the first one said
perguntas.explica: It is a live national argument, not a question you settle.
